title: Hormonal Influences on Female Performance: A Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Study of Cognitive, Motor, and Neuromuscular Function Across the Female Lifespan
summary: Many women report changes such as differences in physical performance, concentration problems or sleep disorders that can affect their everyday lives during various hormonal phases of life, such as the menstrual cycle or the period around the menopause. The aim of the study is to investigate whether these symptoms change as a result of a 12-week health-oriented exercise programme. Women of different ages and stages of life take part in tests to measure neuromuscular, motor and cognitive performance. Some of the participants (intervention group) then complete a 12-week health programme consisting of exercise and workshops in order to record possible changes over time. The results should help to better understand the effects of hormonal life stages and improve future health services for women.

interventions.name: Intervention group: working women (aged 25–65) participating in a 12-week health intervention consisting of an exercise programme (twice a week for 45 minutes) and health workshops on nutrition, sleep and stress.
Control group: working women (aged 25–65) without intervention

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Tracking of the menstrual cycle or menopause status, for which cycle documentation has been carried out for at least 3 months using an app or menstruation diary
- Native-level German language skills
- Written consent to participate in the study and data processing
Exclusion criteria:
- Current pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Occurrence of acute dizziness, fever, infectious diseases or cold symptoms
- Presence of a diagnosed and medically treated mental illness (e.g. major depression) or neurocognitive disorder (e.g. confirmed dementia)
- Presence of a neurological disease (e.g. epilepsy, Parkinson's disease) or traumatic brain injury
- Suffering from severe cardiovascular system limitations (e.g. heart failure, cardiac arrhythmia)
- Impairments of the musculoskeletal system (e.g. immobility, acute pain syndrome, bone diseases, joint replacement), acute injuries to the musculoskeletal system or in the past 6 months
- Orthopaedic surgery in the past 6 months
- Presence of implanted cardiac electrical devices (e.g. pacemaker/ICD)
- Presence of wounds, open skin areas or burns on the upper body in the area of the sternum, upper back or thighs, or skin diseases caused by viruses, fungi or bacteria
- Presence of diabetic neuropathy (e.g. diabetic foot syndrome)
- Harmful use of or dependence on substances, including alcohol
- Presence of speech comprehension disorders
